summary: Processed Snack Food contains BHT requiring caution. Moderate consumption recommended. [1][2]

high_risk.name: BHT (Butylated Hydroxytoluene)
high_risk.micro_report: **  Animal studies indicate BHT acts as an endocrine disruptor, negatively impacting liver, lungs, kidneys, blood, and reproductive systems.  It may also cause liver enlargement and lung inflammation.  Some studies suggest a link to cancer, though this is not definitively proven in humans.

high_risk.name: Artificial Flavors
high_risk.micro_report: ** Certain artificial flavoring compounds have been linked to cancer in animal studies.  Others may cause allergic reactions, digestive issues, and even brain damage. The long-term effects of many artificial flavorings are not fully understood.

high_risk.name: Food Coloring (specifically Red No. 3)
high_risk.micro_report: ** Studies have shown that high doses of Red No. 3 cause tumors in male rats due to a rat-specific hormonal mechanism that does not occur in humans.  While the FDA has banned its use in food products starting in January 2027,  other food dyes may contain cancer-causing contaminants.

moderate_risk.name: High Fructose Corn Syrup
moderate_risk.micro_report: **  Excessive consumption is linked to obesity, fatty liver disease, insulin resistance (increasing type 2 diabetes risk), and inflammation, which is associated with heart disease and cancer.  Moderation is key; avoiding added sugars is generally recommended for better health.

moderate_risk.name: Sugar
moderate_risk.micro_report: **  High sugar intake is associated with weight gain, blood sugar problems, heart disease, stroke, and increased risk of several cancers.  Moderation is crucial; limiting added sugar intake is recommended.

moderate_risk.name: Salt
moderate_risk.micro_report: ** High sodium intake (above recommended daily limits) increases blood pressure, raising the risk of heart disease, stroke, and kidney disease.  Recommended daily intake varies by age and health status, but generally should be limited to less than 2300 mg per day for adults.

moderate_risk.name: Preservatives
moderate_risk.micro_report: ** While some preservatives are safe, many artificial preservatives have been linked to various health problems, including breathing problems, weakened heart tissue, cancer, and obesity.  The long-term effects of many preservatives are not fully understood.  Natural preservatives are generally considered safer.
